durchlauchtigſter Fürſt
Gnädigster Fürst und Herr!
Mein Bothe ist 2 Tage aufgehalten und komt da
er ein Schöps ist heut zurück. Ich ſchicke das
Demme Thier nun auf einen Andern Weg, und melde
Ewr Durchlaucht daß der alte Weigel schon heut
hier bey mir angelangt ist. Er hat nicht nur den
besten Willen den Pacht Contract zu schließen,
sondern er hat mir eröffnet daß er nach meinem
Rath nicht abgeneigt sey die Zagorower Güter
zu kaufen. Er nimmt die Schulden an und
zahlt noch 200000 Rthl zu, diese will er auf
Koschentia abrechnen. Hierbey aber räth er
die Sache verschwiegen zu halten, und Koschentin
subhastiren zu laßen. Er biethet den als
Creditor und hoft es unter der Taxe zu erhalten
was den verlohren geht unß Stössel ver-

verliehren der Ewr Durchlaucht mehr als zu
arg betrogen hätte. Er legagirt ſich einen
Revers auszustellen, daß er Koschentin so
Wie er es erstünde Ewr Durchlaucht oder
wenn Sie es befehlen würden abtreten wolle.
Er glaubt daß Sie es noch unter 600000 Rthl
erhalten würden – Nur müste kein Mensch
ahnden daß Ewr Durchlaucht oder der Fürst
August Koschentin behalten wolte.
Schreiben Ewr durchlaucht mir hierüber
im Geheim Ihre Willensmairung, den der
Alte Mann thut was ich ihm räthe.
die Papiere geruhen Ewr Durchlaucht
nur auf das eiligste zu ſchicken, den ich weiß
mich keinen Rath um die Kosten zu bestreiten
des Instrument muß aber so gestelt sein
wie ichs vorgeschrieben habe ſonst muß es nichts
Ehrfurchtsvoll verharre
Ewr Durchlaucht
Blizanow
d 18ten July 1812
unterthänigſter
v Triebenfeld

translation.en: Most Serene Prince, Most gracious Prince and Lord! My messenger was held up for 2 days and, being a blockhead, is only returning today. I am therefore sending the stupid beast by another route, and report to Your Serene Highness that old Weigel arrived here with me already today. He has not only the best will to conclude the lease contract, but he has disclosed to me that, following my advice, he is not averse to purchasing the Zagorow estates. He assumes the debts and pays a further 200000 Rthl on top, which he wishes to set off against Koschentin. In this, however, he advises that the matter be kept secret, and that Koschentin be put up for compulsory auction. He bids for it as a creditor and hopes to obtain it below the assessed value; what is thereby lost, we lose to Stössel

lose, which would have cheated Your Serene Highness far too grievously. He engages himself to issue a written undertaking that he will cede Koschentin, just as he should acquire it, to Your Serene Highness, or to whomever You should command. He believes that You would obtain it for under 600000 Rthl — only no soul must suspect that Your Serene Highness or Prince August wished to keep Koschentin. Let Your Serene Highness write me Your intention on this in secret, for the old man does what I advise him. As for the papers, may Your Serene Highness be pleased to send them with the greatest haste, for I know no way of meeting the costs; the instrument, however, must be drawn up just as I have prescribed, otherwise it must come to nothing. Reverentially I remain Your Serene Highness's
Blizanow, the 18th of July 1812
most humble and obedient
v Triebenfeld

Most Serene Prince, Most gracious Prince and Lord! My messenger was held up for 2 days and, being a blockhead, is only returning today. I am therefore sending the stupid beast by another route, and report to Your Serene Highness that old Weigel arrived here with me already today. He has not only the best will to conclude the lease contract, but he has disclosed to me that, following my advice, he is not averse to purchasing the Zagorow estates. He assumes the debts and pays a further 200000 Rthl on top, which he wishes to set off against Koschentin. In this, however, he advises that the matter be kept secret, and that Koschentin be put up for compulsory auction. He bids for it as a creditor and hopes to obtain it below the assessed value; what is thereby lost, we lose to Stössel

lose, which would have cheated Your Serene Highness far too grievously. He engages himself to issue a written undertaking that he will cede Koschentin, just as he should acquire it, to Your Serene Highness, or to whomever You should command. He believes that You would obtain it for under 600000 Rthl — only no soul must suspect that Your Serene Highness or Prince August wished to keep Koschentin. Let Your Serene Highness write me Your intention on this in secret, for the old man does what I advise him. As for the papers, may Your Serene Highness be pleased to send them with the greatest haste, for I know no way of meeting the costs; the instrument, however, must be drawn up just as I have prescribed, otherwise it must come to nothing. Reverentially I remain Your Serene Highness's
Blizanow, the 18th of July 1812
most humble and obedient
v Triebenfeld
summary_en: Reports the messenger's two-day delay and his dispatch by another route, then that old Weigel has arrived, is willing to conclude the lease contract and, on Triebenfeld's advice, is not averse to buying the Zagorow estates, assuming the debts and paying a further 200000 Rthl to be set off against Koschentin. Weigel would bid as creditor at a compulsory auction, hoping to secure Koschentin for under 600000 Rthl and cede it back; secrecy from Stössel and others is urged, and the papers are wanted with all haste.
summary_de: Meldet die Verzögerung des Boten und die Ankunft des alten Weigel, der nicht nur den Pachtvertrag abschließen, sondern auf Triebenfelds Rat auch die Zagorower Güter kaufen will: Übernahme der Schulden und weitere 200000 Rthl, die er gegen Koschentin verrechnen möchte. Koschentin solle heimlich zur Zwangsversteigerung kommen, von Weigel als Gläubiger unter Taxe – vermutlich unter 600000 Rthl – erstanden und dem Fürsten schriftlich zediert werden; niemand dürfe Absichten des Fürsten oder des Prinzen August ahnen. Bittet dringend um Übersendung der Papiere.
